scope: The plugin set that `sf commands` lists for the CLI version above: the core plugins that ship with it and the just-in-time plugins it installs on first use. Plugins you install yourself are not in scope.

rules.reason: Shell tab completion for the sf program itself; PowerShell has its own, and a module does not wrap it.
Lists the sf commands. psfdx reads it only to build this report.
Prints sf help for a person at a terminal.
Prints the CLI version; psfdx reads it only for this report and the compatibility lane.
Shows CLI release notes to a person.
Shows CLI release notes to a person.
Tells a person which plugin provides a command.
Interactive search of the CLI command list.
Updates the sf program itself; psfdx installs and updates it with Install-SalesforceCli and Update-SalesforceCli (npm).
Legacy sfdx-style commands kept for old scripts. psfdx wraps the current command that does the same job (see docs/cli-compatibility.md).
Commands for building Salesforce CLI plugins, not for working with an org.
Links a local plugin under development, which only plugin authors do.
Unlinks a local plugin under development, which only plugin authors do.
Prints a live access token. psfdx keeps tokens out of its output; use Connect-SalesforceAccessToken to log in with a token you already have, or Open-Salesforce -UrlOnly for a login link.

Prints the Salesforce DX authorization URL, which holds a refresh token that gives anyone full access as that user. psfdx removes it from every result, including Get-SalesforceOrgDetails, unless -IncludeToken is given.
Prints a user's password. psfdx generates one with New-SalesforceUserPassword and never reads it back from the CLI.
An Agentforce command; it is built with the other agent commands in PSF-61.
An Agentforce command; it is built with the other agent commands in PSF-61.
--sfdx-url-stdin reads the URL from standard input, which Invoke-Salesforce cannot feed; -SfdxUrlFile covers the same login.
GET is what the CLI uses when --method is left out, and psfdx leaves it out for reads; the CLI data does not record that default.
